prompts: Original Japanese top-down pixel RPG asset visually inspired by Pokemon FireRed's overworld. Orthographic three-quarter TOP-DOWN RPG angle, front facing directly down to player, no isometric diamond or perspective convergence. Chunky deliberate pixels, crisp edges, restrained 24-color palette, dark colored outlines, sun from upper left, simple 3-shade clusters. Transparent background, no floor, no shadow beyond footprint, no text or logos. Readable when scaled down into a 16px-grid game. Match the attached reference sprites exactly in palette, outline and pixel density. pixel-art game sprite of the real storefront; not resembling any Nintendo / Game Freak / Pokémon asset. Override no-logo rule for required McDonald's brand. Attached images are style references. Match the palette, outline weight, pixel density and three-quarter top-down angle of the attached reference sprites exactly. ONE isolated Japanese McDonald's restaurant sprite. 112x80 logical pixel grid enlarged to >=1024px wide. Single story with flat cream/slate roof visible above, bright RED facade sign with a single BIG golden yellow iconic McDonald's M arches mark. Brand mark must be unmistakable at 1x. Dark window frames, glass front, central glass entrance door. No other lettering necessary. Small warm cream side columns. Front faces down square to screen, no isometric view. No ground, people, cars or shadow outside footprint. Fill canvas with 2 logical pixel margin. Crisp dark colored outlines and bold simple 3-shade pixel clusters.
notes: Real brand storefront by art-direction decision (#85); not affiliated. Anchors are zero-based runtime pixel coordinates from top-left. Door marks the threshold; foot marks the bottom-centre sorting point. collisionTiles is the 16px-grid ground footprint of the facade (roof overhang and transparent padding are not collision). Atlas is the artist-finished exact-size sprite: alpha>=128 crop, nearest-neighbour fit, quantized to <=31 colours + transparent, hard alpha. Map owner places a walkable portal in front of the door. Art reviewed at 1x and 3x/6x.
